user_query: Applicant seems vulnerable — how do I assess this and adapt my response?
variations: Applicant says a social worker told them to call.
Applicant has a disability that affects their ability to seek help.
part_a_general_info: Vulnerability affects (a) how you conduct the call (pace, language, patience) and (b) which scheme pathway is appropriate. You do NOT ask the applicant directly "are you vulnerable?" — you assess from cues and, where natural, use the sensitively-worded probes in Part B. If two or more factors are present, or any single severe factor (e.g., minor, ongoing violence, FSC-referred), treat as HIGH-vulnerability and escalate. Vulnerability factors to listen for: • Violence victim (current or recent) • Elderly applicant with apparent confusion or isolation • Technology-illiterate (cannot use email, apps, online forms) • Language barrier (limited English and no other listed language handled) • Minor (under 18) • Already engaged with an FSC social worker • Basic needs at risk (food, shelter, money) • Physical or cognitive disability affecting independent action Scheme implications: vulnerable applicants may qualify for the Community Law Centre (free legal consultation, usually by in-house team who can provide greater support). High-vulnerability cases should be escalated to PBSG Staff (Route F of GEN3-T01) for hand-holding.
triage_questions: Q1: "To make sure I understand your situation — are you speaking for yourself today, or did someone help you make this call?" (Probes: caregiver involvement, third-party influence, language assistance.)
Q2: "Is there anything about how we're speaking today that would make it easier for you — for example, would you prefer a different language, or should I speak more slowly?"
Q3: "Are you currently safe where you are, and do you have a safe place to stay tonight?"
Q4: "Are you currently working with a social worker, counsellor, or case officer on anything?"
Q5: "Can I just check — are you 18 or older?" (Only ask if age is genuinely unclear. Do not ask applicants who are obviously adult.)
Q6: "Is there anything I should know that would help me help you better — any health, mobility, or access concerns?"

Q1.question: "To make sure I understand your situation — are you speaking for yourself today, or did someone help you make this call?" (Probes: caregiver involvement, third-party influence, language assistance.)
Q1.if_helper_present: Note who; ask permission to continue with applicant directly.

Q2.question: "Is there anything about how we're speaking today that would make it easier for you — for example, would you prefer a different language, or should I speak more slowly?"
Q2.action: Record language preference. If not one PBSG handles, note for escalation to interpreter.

Q3.question: "Are you currently safe where you are, and do you have a safe place to stay tonight?"

Q4.question: "Are you currently working with a social worker, counsellor, or case officer on anything?"
Q4.if_yes: Ask for the FSC or organisation name; treat as HIGH-vulnerability; coordinate rather than duplicate.

Q5.question: "Can I just check — are you 18 or older?" (Only ask if age is genuinely unclear. Do not ask applicants who are obviously adult.)

Q6.question: "Is there anything I should know that would help me help you better — any health, mobility, or access concerns?"
Q6.action: Note any disclosed disability or accessibility need.

routing_rules.if_2_or_more_cues_or_severe_single_facto: Route A (High-Vulnerability — Escalate + Community Law Centre). Severe factors: minor, active violence, FSC-referred.
routing_rules.if_1_cue_non_severe: Route C (Low-Vulnerability — Standard Triage with Adaptations).
routing_rules.if_unclear: Route A (Escalate to PBSG Staff for professional assessment).

routing: Route A (High-Vulnerability — Escalate + Community Law Centre): Take down full intake particulars + vulnerability factors noted. Escalate to PBSG Staff for further assessment and active follow-up. If applicant is able to communicate their issue, proceed with standard triage (GEN3-T01) but note that routes may be adjusted by staff.

Route B (Minor — Special Handling): Do NOT continue the triage independently. Escalate immediately to PBSG Staff. Do not ask the minor for sensitive disclosures beyond what they have volunteered. If the minor indicates any immediate safety concern, follow GEN3-T06 Route A.

Route C (Low-Vulnerability — Standard Triage with Adaptations): Continue with GEN3-T01, but: (a) slow your pace; (b) repeat scheme names and URLs; (c) offer to email a summary after the call; (d) do not rush the applicant. Flag the call in the intake note with the cue observed, for staff awareness.

Route A.name: High-Vulnerability — Escalate + Community Law Centre
Route A.script: I want to make sure we handle this carefully. Let me take down the key details and have PBSG Staff assess the best way to follow up with you.
needs_to_know: Use this route when there are two or more vulnerability factors, or one severe factor such as a minor, active violence, or FSC-referred applicant.
PBSG Staff may assess whether the Community Law Centre or another supported pathway is appropriate.
prepare: Brief legal matter description if the applicant can communicate it
intern_steps: Take down full intake particulars and the vulnerability factors noted.
Escalate to PBSG Staff for further assessment and active follow-up.
If the applicant can communicate their issue, continue standard triage through GEN3-T01 and flag that staff may adjust the route.
caveats: Do not ask intrusive vulnerability questions beyond what is necessary for routing and safety.

Route B.name: Minor — Special Handling
Route B.script: I need PBSG Staff to handle this carefully. I will not ask you for more sensitive details right now, but I will escalate this immediately.
needs_to_know: Use this route when the applicant is confirmed to be under 18.
prepare: Any safety concern the minor has already volunteered
intern_steps: Do not ask the minor for sensitive disclosures beyond what they have volunteered.
If there is any immediate safety concern, follow GEN3-T06 Route A.
caveats: Protect the minor's safety and confidentiality.

Route C.name: Low-Vulnerability — Standard Triage with Adaptations
Route C.script: I can continue with the usual triage questions. I will go slowly, repeat key details, and can help summarise the next steps after the call.
needs_to_know: Use this route when there is one non-severe vulnerability cue and no immediate safety or high-vulnerability concern.
prepare: Any communication preference or access need
intern_steps: Slow your pace and do not rush the applicant.
Repeat scheme names and URLs where helpful.
Offer to email a summary after the call.
Flag the observed cue in the intake note for staff awareness.
caveats: Escalate if new vulnerability or safety cues appear.

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
